entries.title: Jeremiah 25:1
segments: The fourth year of Jehoiakim--the first year of Nebuchadrezzar; the first year of Nebuchadnezzar seems to have corresponded partly with the third and partly with the fourth year of Jehoiakim. Compare
. This prophecy was delivered earlier than that recorded in the preceding chapter, the arrangement of the writings of Jeremiah, here and elsewhere, not preserving the chronological order.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:8
segments:
vv 8,11. 
 
Though God's judgments be long delayed, they will come at last upon the incorrigibly impenitent, and their severity will be in proportion to the exhortations and warnings that have been despised.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:9
segments: These nations round about; the nations afterwards enumerated,

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:10
segments: The sound of the millstones; the millstones of the hand-mill, in which the people of the East daily grind their meal.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:11
segments: Seventy years; generally reckoned from the first invasion of the land by Nebuchadnezzar during the reign of Jehoiakim, when the process of transportation to Babylon began.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:12
segments: However sore the chastisement which God inflicts upon his people, he remembers them at the appointed time in mercy; and their cruel and relentless persecutors he destroys.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:13
segments: This book--against all the nations; "this book" seems to refer to the whole connection of Jeremiah's writings.  The more distinguished prophecies "against all the nations" now stand in the last part of the book.  We must suppose either that they were originally written at an earlier date, or, what is more probable, that the present clause was added in arranging the whole volume.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:15
segments: The wine-cup of this fury; here, as often elsewhere, God's wrath is compared to an intoxicating wine-cup, which makes those who drink it mad, and causes them to stagger and fall.

vv 15-28, 30-33. 
 
God's power over the human family is unlimited; it is as easy for him to send forth desolating calamities from nation to nation over all the earth, as to punish the weakest transgressor of his laws.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:16
segments: Be moved; reel.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:17
segments: Then took I the cup; this was plainly done only in prophetic vision.  He makes the nations to drink by announcing God's wrath that is coming upon them.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:18
segments:
vv 18-26. 
 
  Jerusalem--all the kings of the Medes; all these nations were to be destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar. 
 
  The mingled people; probably here, as in

, the mixed mass of foreigners serving the Egyptians. 
 
  Uz; probably situated in the northern part of Arabia. 
 
  The isles--beyond the sea; the western islands of the Mediterranean, with the adjacent coasts. 
 
Dedan, and Tema, and Buz; in the northern part of Arabia. 
 
  All--in the utmost corners; see note on

. 
 
  Zimri; an unknown tribe, probably lying in the direction of Persia and Media. 
 
  Elam; Persia. 
 
  The Medes; northeast of Persia, and south and west of the Captain. 
 
  All the kings of the north; the Scythian tribes north of the Euxine and Black sea. 
 
  All the kingdoms of the world; in a general sense.  Compare

. 
 
  Sheshach; a name for Babylon.
After God has used the king of Babylon as the minister of his wrath upon these nations, he shall in turn be destroyed.  Compare what is said of Assyria,

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:29
segments: The judgments which God brings upon his offending people are a solemn warning to the wicked of the more terrible vengeance which will one day fall upon them.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:31
segments: A noise shall come; the tumult of warlike hosts, under the marshalling of Jehovah.  Compare

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:34
segments:
Shepherds--principal of the flock; the nobles and rulers of the nations. 
 
  Are accomplished; have fully come.

Like a pleasant vessel; as a costly vessel falls and is dashed in pieces. 
 
vv 34-38. 
 
It is a righteous rule of divine Providence, that wicked leaders of the people, who are first in crime, should be first also in suffering, when he punishes nations for their sins.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:36
segments: Spoiled their pasture; destroyed their land and people.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:37
segments: Cut down; desolated.

entries.title: Jeremiah 25:38
segments: He hath forsaken; Jehovah, as the leader of the conquering hosts, who is here compared to a lion.
